exercises.title: Remove while iterating: Iterator.remove on any List
exercises.problemHtml:
Complete static int removeIf(List<Integer> list, int divisor): remove every element divisible by divisor and return how many were removed. The list may be an ArrayList or a LinkedList — the grader tries both.

Two classic mistakes: removing inside a for-each loop throws ConcurrentModificationException; a loop with list.get(i) / list.remove(i) is O(n) per call on a LinkedList, O(n²) overall. Walk with an Iterator and call it.remove().

⏱ Complexity check. One case runs your code on a large input (n = 300,000 elements of a LinkedList, half removed) inside a 3-second limit. An O(n) solution finishes in a fraction of a second on any ordinary laptop; an O(n²) with get(i)/remove(i) one needs far longer and the case prints TOO SLOW. On a LinkedList, get(i) and remove(i) walk from an end every time. The limit is generous on purpose — if it fails, the algorithm is the problem, not your machine.

Run the grader on your machine

The website does NOT grade this exercise. Press Tải .zip (download) above the code, unzip it, edit the code in src/, then inside the exercise folder (the one with cham.mjs) run:

node cham.mjs

The zip unpacks into a folder named after the exercise (<folder> below). Windows (PowerShell): cd "$env:USERPROFILE\Downloads\<folder>" — cmd: cd /d %USERPROFILE%\Downloads\<folder> — then node cham.mjs. macOS (Terminal): cd ~/Downloads/<folder> then node cham.mjs. Tip: type cd and drag the folder into the terminal window. You need Node.js 18+ and JDK 8 or newer (17 or 21 recommended) — javac -version must work.

The grader compiles src/ with javac, runs 3 case(s) (2 hidden — not printed in this text), compares your output line by line (trailing spaces and Windows/macOS line endings ignored), prints a diff of the wrong lines, checks the source rules and gives a score. When it prints ALL CHECKS PASSED, come back and press Tự đánh dấu đã giải (self-mark as solved). node cham.mjs --case 2 --show prints the input and your whole output for case 2.

Requirements

  • Do not use List.removeIf or streams — write the iterator loop yourself (rule R1).
  • Do not copy into another list.
exercises.problemHtmlVi:
Hoàn thiện static int removeIf(List<Integer> list, int divisor): xoá mọi phần tử chia hết cho divisor và trả về số phần tử đã xoá. Danh sách có thể là ArrayList hoặc LinkedList — máy chấm thử cả hai.

Hai lỗi kinh điển: xoá trong vòng for-each ném ConcurrentModificationException; vòng lặp dùng list.get(i) / list.remove(i) tốn O(n) mỗi lần trên LinkedList, tổng O(n²). Hãy duyệt bằng Iterator và gọi it.remove().

⏱ Kiểm độ phức tạp. Một ca chạy code của bạn với input LỚN (n = 300,000 elements of a LinkedList, half removed) trong hạn 3 giây. Lời giải O(n) xong trong chưa tới một giây trên laptop bình thường; bản O(n²) with get(i)/remove(i) cần lâu hơn rất nhiều và ca in TOO SLOW. Trên LinkedList, get(i) và remove(i) mỗi lần đều đi từ một đầu. Hạn đặt rộng có chủ ý — trượt ca này thì do thuật toán, không phải do máy bạn.

exercises.solutionExplanationHtml: The iterator remembers where it stands: on a LinkedList, it.remove() unlinks that node in O(1), so the whole pass is O(n). On an ArrayList each it.remove() still shifts the tail (O(n²) worst case, but with a fast memory move) — the same code is optimal for linked lists and correct for both.
exercises.solutionExplanationHtmlVi: Iterator nhớ mình đang đứng ở đâu: trên LinkedList, it.remove() gỡ nút đó trong O(1), nên cả lượt là O(n). Trên ArrayList mỗi it.remove() vẫn dời phần đuôi (xấu nhất O(n²), nhưng bằng phép chép bộ nhớ nhanh) — cùng một đoạn code tối ưu cho danh sách liên kết và đúng cho cả hai.

mistakesJson.loi: for (Integer x : list) list.remove(x) — ConcurrentModificationException (and remove(Object) vs remove(int index) confusion).|||for (Integer x : list) list.remove(x) — ConcurrentModificationException (lại còn nhầm remove(Object) với remove(int index)).

for (int i = 0; i < list.size(); i++) with remove(i) — skips the element that slides into slot i, and is O(n²) on a LinkedList.|||for (int i = 0; i < list.size(); i++) kèm remove(i) — bỏ sót phần tử trượt vào ô i, và O(n²) trên LinkedList.

exercises.title: Merge two sorted Lists with iterators, whatever their class
exercises.problemHtml:
Complete static List<Integer> merge(List<Integer> a, List<Integer> b): both inputs are sorted ascending; return a new ArrayList with every element of both, sorted, equal values from a before those from b. Do not change the inputs.

The inputs can be LinkedLists, so a.get(i) is O(i): use iterators and keep the "current" element of each list in a variable.

⏱ Complexity check. One case runs your code on a large input (n = 2 × 200,000 elements in LinkedLists) inside a 3-second limit. An O(n + m) solution finishes in a fraction of a second on any ordinary laptop; an O(n²) with get(i) one needs far longer and the case prints TOO SLOW. Indexing a LinkedList walks from an end each time. The limit is generous on purpose — if it fails, the algorithm is the problem, not your machine.

Run the grader on your machine

The website does NOT grade this exercise. Press Tải .zip (download) above the code, unzip it, edit the code in src/, then inside the exercise folder (the one with cham.mjs) run:

Tip: type cd and drag the folder into the terminal window. You need Node.js 18+ and JDK 8 or newer (17 or 21 recommended) — javac -version must work.

The grader compiles src/ with javac, runs 3 case(s) (2 hidden — not printed in this text), compares your output line by line (trailing spaces and Windows/macOS line endings ignored), prints a diff of the wrong lines, checks the source rules and gives a score. When it prints ALL CHECKS PASSED, come back and press Tự đánh dấu đã giải (self-mark as solved). node cham.mjs --case 2 --show prints the input and your whole output for case 2.

  • O(n + m): no get(i), no sort (rule R1).

exercises.title: Pick the right structure: a ticket queue of 400,000 customers
exercises.problemHtml:
TicketDesk hands out numbers and serves customers in order. The starter keeps the waiting customers in an ArrayList and serves with remove(0) — every service shifts the whole list. Rewrite the class with a Deque<Integer> (ArrayDeque) so that arrive(), serve() and waiting() are O(1):

  • int arrive() — the next ticket number (1, 2, 3, …) joins the back of the queue and is returned;
  • int serve() — the front ticket leaves and is returned; −1 when nobody waits;
  • int waiting(), String peekAll() — the queue as "[3, 4, 5]".

⏱ Complexity check. One case runs your code on a large input (n = 400,000 arrivals then 400,000 services) inside a 3-second limit. An O(1) per operation solution finishes in a fraction of a second on any ordinary laptop; an O(n) per serve (ArrayList.remove(0)) one needs far longer and the case prints TOO SLOW. remove(0) shifts every waiting customer: about 8·10¹⁰ element moves. The limit is generous on purpose — if it fails, the algorithm is the problem, not your machine.

Run the grader on your machine

The website does NOT grade this exercise. Press Tải .zip (download) above the code, unzip it, edit the code in src/, then inside the exercise folder (the one with cham.mjs) run:

node cham.mjs

The zip unpacks into a folder named after the exercise (<folder> below). Windows (PowerShell): cd "$env:USERPROFILE\Downloads\<folder>" — cmd: cd /d %USERPROFILE%\Downloads\<folder> — then node cham.mjs. macOS (Terminal): cd ~/Downloads/<folder> then node cham.mjs. Tip: type cd and drag the folder into the terminal window. You need Node.js 18+ and JDK 8 or newer (17 or 21 recommended) — javac -version must work.

The grader compiles src/ with javac, runs 2 case(s) (0 hidden — not printed in this text), compares your output line by line (trailing spaces and Windows/macOS line endings ignored), prints a diff of the wrong lines, checks the source rules and gives a score. When it prints ALL CHECKS PASSED, come back and press Tự đánh dấu đã giải (self-mark as solved). node cham.mjs --case 2 --show prints the input and your whole output for case 2.

Requirements

  • No ArrayList in TicketDesk (rule R1).
  • Same behaviour as the starter.

exercises.solutionExplanationHtml: ArrayList.remove(0) moves every remaining element one slot left: O(n) per service, O(n²) for the day. ArrayDeque keeps head and tail indexes in a circular array, so both ends are O(1) — the structure the Java documentation recommends for queues and stacks.
exercises.solutionExplanationHtmlVi: ArrayList.remove(0) dời mọi phần tử còn lại sang trái một ô: O(n) mỗi lần phục vụ, O(n²) cả ngày. ArrayDeque giữ chỉ số đầu và cuối trên mảng vòng nên cả hai đầu O(1) — cấu trúc tài liệu Java khuyên dùng cho hàng đợi và ngăn xếp.

mistakesJson.loi: Keeping List<Integer> and switching to LinkedList but still calling get(0)/remove(0) through an index loop elsewhere — fine here, but the interface Deque says what you mean.|||Giữ List<Integer> rồi đổi sang LinkedList nhưng nơi khác vẫn gọi get(i) theo chỉ số — ở đây thì qua, nhưng interface Deque nói đúng ý bạn hơn.

Using push/pop of the Deque — they work at the FRONT (stack order), so the last customer would be served first.|||Dùng push/pop của Deque — chúng làm việc ở ĐẦU (thứ tự ngăn xếp), nên khách đến sau được phục vụ trước.
